title: The last bus home
summary: A night bus driver has seen almost everything, until one passenger changes his routine.
paragraphs: For eleven years, Fermín had driven the last night bus in the city, the N4, which left the centre at half past one and reached the hospital at the top of the hill at ten past two. He knew every stop, every {{pothole}} and most of his passengers: the cleaners going to the offices, the nurses finishing their shifts, the students who had missed the metro, the musicians carrying their instruments home.

He had seen almost everything on that bus. Couples arguing, people crying, a man who brought a live chicken in a box, a group of tourists who sang the whole way and gave him a bottle of wine. Usually, he said little. He drove carefully, said "good night" at every stop and listened to the radio quietly.

Then, one winter, a new passenger appeared. She was about seventy and got on at the stop by the river at twenty to two, every night, with a small bag. She always sat behind him and got off at the hospital. After a week, Fermín was {{curious}}. After two weeks, he was worried. One night he asked, "Are you visiting someone?" She told him that her husband was in hospital, and that she sat with him every night because he couldn't sleep when he was alone.

From then on, they talked every night for twenty minutes. She told him about her husband, who had been a fisherman, and about their fifty years together. Fermín told her about his daughter, who was studying in Germany. When it rained, he stopped the bus a little closer to the hospital door, although it wasn't {{exactly}} allowed.

In March, she stopped coming. Fermín didn't know what had happened, and he felt a strange {{emptiness}} at the river stop. Three weeks later, she got on the bus again, in the afternoon, when a colleague was driving and Fermín was a passenger going to a {{training}} course. She was smiling. Her husband had come home. She had a box of cakes, and she had been trying to find Fermín for days to give them to him.

pothole.meaning: a hole in the surface of a road

curious.meaning: wanting to know or learn about something

exactly.meaning: completely or perfectly; here, in a way that follows the rules completely

training.meaning: the process of learning the skills for a job

emptiness.meaning: a feeling that something is missing

He has driven the last night bus for eleven years.
